paper.title: Tensile deformation behavior analysis of low density Fe–18Mn–10Al–xC steels
paper.paper_scope: Investigates how carbon content (0.5, 0.8 and 1.2 wt%) changes the as-quenched microstructure of low density Fe–18Mn–10Al–xC steels and how these microstructural differences control tensile deformation and multi-stage strain hardening behavior, analyzed via Crussard–Jaoul (C–J) analysis and interrupted tensile tests.

alloys.description: Low density Fe–Mn–Al–C steel; in the as-quenched state it has a duplex ferritic–austenitic microstructure with an austenite volume fraction of 59.2% and no precipitates in either the austenite or ferrite phase.
alloys.alloys_notes: Nominal design composition Fe–18Mn–10Al–0.5C (wt%). Measured chemical composition (mass%): Al 9.90, Mn 17.71, C 0.48, Fe Bal. (Table 1). Calculated density 6.92 g/cm3; austenite stacking fault energy (SFE) 73.4 mJ/m2.

source.reason: The paper selects three Fe–18Mn–10Al–xC steels with 0.5, 0.8 and 1.2 C (wt%) as distinct alloy compositions; Table 1 lists the chemical composition of the '0.5C' steel, which is a separate alloy composition from the 0.8C and 1.2C steels.

alloys.description: Low density Fe–Mn–Al–C steel; as-quenched it has a duplex ferritic–austenitic structure with an austenite fraction of 84.8%, containing ordered phases (B2 with fine DO3 particles in ferrite, κ carbide in austenite). Because both ferrite and austenite contain ordered phases it is referred to as a 'complex low density steel'.
alloys.alloys_notes: Nominal design composition Fe–18Mn–10Al–0.8C (wt%). Measured chemical composition (mass%): Al 9.91, Mn 17.14, C 0.77, Fe Bal. (Table 1). Calculated density 6.88 g/cm3; austenite SFE 77.9 mJ/m2. Both ferrite (B2 + DO3) and austenite (κ carbide) contain ordered phases.

source.reason: Table 1 lists the '0.8C' steel as a distinct composition (C 0.77 wt%) separate from the 0.5C and 1.2C steels; the paper repeatedly treats the 0.8C steel as its own alloy, describing it as a 'complex low density steel' with ordered phases in both phases.

alloys.description: Low density Fe–Mn–Al–C steel; as-quenched it is fully austenitic with some annealing twins and κ carbides [(Fe,Mn)3AlCx] uniformly distributed in the austenite matrix.
alloys.alloys_notes: Nominal design composition Fe–18Mn–10Al–1.2C (wt%). Measured chemical composition (mass%): Al 10.19, Mn 17.45, C 1.16, Fe Bal. (Table 1). Calculated density 6.78 g/cm3; austenite SFE 84.5 mJ/m2.

source.reason: Table 1 lists the '1.2C' steel as a distinct composition (C 1.16 wt%) separate from the 0.5C and 0.8C steels; the abstract and results describe it as a fully austenitic microstructure with κ carbides, a distinct alloy from the duplex/complex steels.

processes.process_name: 1000 °C annealing followed by water quenching (as-quenched state)
processes.description: The steels were prepared by induction melting (50 kg ingots, argon), forged at 1200 °C, hot rolled after homogenization at 1200 °C for 3 h to 3.5 mm (90% reduction), annealed at 1000 °C for 1 h, cold rolled to 1 mm, then finally annealed at 1000 °C and water quenched to room temperature, giving the as-quenched terminal state.
processes.processes_notes: This identical thermo-mechanical/heating route was applied to all three Fe–18Mn–10Al–xC steels; the resulting terminal as-quenched state is shared across the three alloys, so alloy_id is left null (the process is not specific to a single alloy).

This sample is the intersection of the 0.5C alloy composition (Table 1) with the shared as-quenched terminal state (1000 °C anneal + water quench) described in block b0016 and referred to as as-quenched in block b0020.

unmapped_findings: Calculated densities of the three steels: 6.92, 6.88 and 6.78 g/cm3 for the 0.5C, 0.8C and 1.2C steels, respectively (block b0016).
Stacking fault energy (SFE) values of austenite: 73.4 and 77.9 mJ/m2 for the 0.5C and 0.8C steels, and 84.5 mJ/m2 for the 1.2C steel (block b0016).

Tensile properties (Table 2, block b0037): 0.5C — TE 32.8%, YS 614.9 MPa, UTS 856.7 MPa, UTS×TE 28100 MPa·%; 0.8C — TE 38.4%, YS 711.2 MPa, UTS 979.1 MPa, UTS×TE 37597 MPa·%; 1.2C — TE 56.2%, YS 735.1 MPa, UTS 946.7 MPa, UTS×TE 53205 MPa·%.

Tensile tests were carried out at room temperature on a universal testing machine (SANSCMT5000) at constant crosshead displacement velocity equivalent to an initial strain rate of 1.33×10^-3 s^-1 (block b0017).

Strain-hardening behavior: 0.5C and 0.8C steels exhibit a two-stage strain hardening, while the 1.2C steel exhibits a three-stage strain hardening by Crussard–Jaoul (C–J) analysis (blocks b0025, b0051, b0062).
